To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the antinucleus-to-nucleus ratios are consistent with the thermal freeze-out hypothesis, and that the antinuclear-to-nuclear ratios are consistent with a coalescence production mechanism.

“The production of antinuclei is consistent with the coalescence of nucleons from a thermalized source with a temperature of ~ 120 MeV, while the production of nuclei requires a source with a temperature lower than ~ 100 MeV.”
nuclei and antineutrons in Pb+P
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the production of nuclei and antinuclei in Pb+P collisions.
the production of nuclei and antinuclei in heavy ion collisions.
a detailed investigation of the production mechanism of nuclei and antinuci in high energy collisions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the antideuterons and anti-tritons are produced by the coalescence of thermalized hadrons, while the antihelium-3 and antihelium 4 are produced by the fragmentation of thermalized hadronic matter.
the production mechanism of antinuclei, as well as of nuclei, in Pb+PB collisions at 158A GeV is the coalescence of thermalized hadrons at freeze-out.
the production mechanism of light nuclei and antinuclei is mainly due to a coalescence process, which occurs after a thermal freeze-out, at the same time as for the hadrons.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have investigated the production mechanism of nuclei and antinucelis in heavy-ion collisions at 158 AGeV, which are mainly produced via coalescence mechanism.
the production of light antinuclei (and nuclei) is a coalescence process from the hadronic phase of the collision.
the production of nuclei and antinuclei in Pb+P
The main takeaway from our work is that
the coalescence of hadrons is the dominant mechanism of nuclei production in Pb+Pbv collisions at 158A GeV.
the coalescence model is a powerful tool to investigate the properties of the hadronization phase.
the coalescence model is a very successful model in describing the production of nuclei and antinucei in Pb+ Pb collisions at the SPS.
